title: Real Research Today: Conversational Compilers
definition: Today's documented research behind Conversational Compilers.
description:
The road to Conversational Compilers is already being paved. Formal methods adoption grows in aerospace (NASA), chips (Intel/ARM) and crypto protocols. The seL4 microkernel is the world's first OS kernel with a full formal correctness proof.

The Lean theorem prover and Coq/Isabelle communities verify real software mathematically. Together these programs form the dialogue passes foundation that Conversational Compilers will build on — the compiler logistics results, the error conversations methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as compiler logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Conversational Compilers Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Conversational Compilers: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Conversational Compilers — compilers that discuss code with you as they build.

Phase 1 — Prove (dialogue passes): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (compiler logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (error conversations): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (fix proposals): compiler hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and developers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
